style: High-energy, aggressive transition team under Jesse Marsch, pressing intensely and attacking with pace down the flanks. Direct, vertical play built to exploit space behind opposition defences.
recent_form: Co-hosts entering the World Cup with momentum and home advantage. Opened Group B but managing an Alphonso Davies hamstring injury that affected his availability for the opener.

key_players.name: Alphonso Davies
key_players.note: Bayern Munich star and the face of Canadian football; explosive pace, though hampered by a hamstring injury at the tournament.

key_players.name: Jonathan David
key_players.note: Juventus forward and Canada's all-time leading scorer; clinical focal point of the attack.

key_players.name: Stephen Eustáquio
key_players.note: Provides stability, tempo control and leadership in midfield.

key_players.name: Tajon Buchanan
key_players.note: Versatile flank attacker with pace, creativity and directness on either side.

key_players.name: Alistair Johnston
key_players.note: Energetic, defensively reliable full-back who contributes going forward.

key_players.name: Moïse Bombito
key_players.note: Athletic, physical defender expected to play a major role at the back.

historical_news: Canada is co-hosting the 2026 World Cup alongside the USA and Mexico.
Alphonso Davies captains the side but battled a hamstring injury into the tournament.
Jonathan David enters as Canada's all-time leading scorer after moving to Juventus.
Jesse Marsch leads an ambitious side aiming to progress beyond the group stage on home soil.
Canada drawn in Group B, opening against Bosnia and Herzegovina.

media_sentiment.label: positive
media_sentiment.summary: Hopeful tone driven by home advantage and a talented attacking core, tempered by concern over Davies's fitness.
